portion_rule.text: The recipe macros are shown per base serving = Person 2's plate. Person 1 hits his higher target by adding the listed extras each meal (typically +1 scoop whey or extra dal/curd at breakfast, and +1 cup cooked rice OR +2 rotis at lunch and dinner). Roughly: Person 2 eats the base plate; Person 1 eats the base plate ×1.4.
portion_rule.hindi: Khana ek saath banega. Person 2 normal plate lega, Person 1 usi plate me thoda extra roti/rice aur protein add karega.
portion_rule.how_to_use: Cooking is shared — recipes make enough for both people. Because Person 1 needs more energy and protein than Person 2, each meal lists a base serving (Person 2's portion) and simple Person 1 add-ons (extra roti/rice + a protein topper).
portion_rule.plating_tip: Portion as you cook: plate Person 2's base serving first, then add Person 1's extras to the pan/plate — keeps macros on track without weighing every day.

disclaimer: This plan is for general education and healthy adults. It is not medical or personalised dietetic advice. Anyone with a medical condition, or who is pregnant/breastfeeding, should consult a doctor or registered dietitian before starting.

Heat a non-stick tawa, pour a ladle, spread thin, drizzle a little oil, cook both sides till golden.
Makes ~4 chillas.
Serve with curd.

targets.method: Maintenance calories are estimated with the Mifflin–St Jeor equation and an activity factor for 4 training days plus daily walking. A moderate calorie deficit is used so that fat is lost while muscle is protected by high protein and hard training.
targets.before_you_start: Weigh yourself once at the beginning and then weekly (same time, morning, after toilet, before eating). Judge progress over 2–3 weeks, not day to day — water weight fluctuates. If a woman is pregnant, breastfeeding, or anyone has a medical condition, check with a doctor before starting a deficit or new training.

person1.title: Person 1 (Male, Intermediate) — Upper / Lower (4 days)
person1.why: For an intermediate lifter who wants to keep strength while losing fat, an Upper/Lower split is the best fit. Each muscle is trained twice a week, which is ideal for building/keeping muscle, and it's simple to run in a normal gym.
person1.rest: Wed, Sat, Sun off (or light walk)
person1.warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike/incline walk) → arm circles, leg swings, band pull-aparts 2×15 → then for your first main lift do 2 light ramp-up sets: empty bar ×10, then ~50% of working weight ×5.
person1.warmup_hindi: Pehle halka set lagao, phir working weight — chot nahi lagegi.
rules: RPE = how hard a set feels. RPE 7 ≈ 3 reps left in the tank, RPE 8 ≈ 2 left, RPE 9 ≈ 1 left, RPE 10 = failure.
Weekly intensity: Week 1 = RPE 7 (leave 3 reps), Week 2 = RPE 8, Week 3 = RPE 8.5–9 (hardest), Week 4 = Deload (~60% weight, half the sets).

When to increase WEIGHT: if you hit the top of the rep range on all sets with good form and it still felt like the target RPE (or easier), add weight next time — +2.5 kg on upper-body lifts, +5 kg on squat/deadlift.
When to increase REPS: if you can't add weight yet, keep the weight and add 1 rep per set until you reach the top of the range, then add weight.

After failing a set (missed reps / form broke): rack it — don't grind ugly reps. Rest a bit longer, drop the weight ~10% and finish your remaining sets at target reps. Keep the same weight next session and try again. Only lower the program weight if you miss it 2 sessions in a row.
Double progression rule: stay at a weight until you hit the top of the rep range on every set, then jump up.
person1.notation: Sets × Reps @RPE. Tempo shown as e.g. 3-0-1 = 3 s down, 0 pause, 1 s up. Rest in minutes.

weeks.2: Week 2 — RPE 8 (add load). Same exercises and rep ranges. Push to RPE 8 (leave ~2 reps). Add +2.5 kg to upper lifts and +5 kg to squat/deadlift wherever you hit the top of the range last week. Big lifts approx: Bench ~50 kg, Squat ~60 kg, Deadlift ~95 kg, aiming for the same rep targets. Optional: add 1 set to Bench and Squat if recovery is good.
weeks.3: Week 3 — RPE 8.5–9 (peak, hardest week). Heaviest, most demanding week. Reps live at the lower end of each range but heavier. Leave only ~1 rep in the tank on top sets. Big lifts approx: Bench ~52.5 kg, Squat ~65 kg, Deadlift ~100 kg (adjust to feel, not ego). Rest an extra 30–60 s on main lifts. If a set drops below the min reps, that's your ceiling — hold it, don't force.
weeks.4: Week 4 — DELOAD (recover & grow). Use ~60% of your Week-3 weights, drop to 2 sets per exercise, stop every set at RPE 5–6 (easy). Skip the smallest isolation moves (lateral raise, face pull, calf, curl, ab work if tired). Keep protein and steps high. Goal: move well, feel fresh by Sunday.

person2.title: Person 2 (Female, Beginner) — Upper / Lower (4 days, beginner-friendly)
person2.why: Same simple Upper/Lower layout, but with machines and easy-to-learn movements first. The focus for Weeks 1–2 is learning good form with light weight, then adding load.
person2.warmup: 5 min brisk walk/bike → 10 bodyweight squats, 10 glute bridges, arm circles, band pull-aparts 2×15. On your first machine, do 1 light set of 12 to groove the movement.
person2.warmup_hindi: Pehle bina weight ke movement practice karo.
rules: RPE feel: Week 1 = RPE 6–7 (very doable, 3–4 reps left), Week 2 = RPE 7, Week 3 = RPE 8 (2 left), Week 4 = Deload (easy).
Increase reps first: start at the bottom of the range; each session try to add 1–2 reps until you reach the top of the range on all sets.
Then increase weight: once you hit the top of the range on all sets with good form, add the smallest jump — +1–2.5 kg (machines/dumbbells) or the next pin — and drop back to the bottom of the range.
After failing a set: no problem — rack it, rest, lower the weight a little, and finish your reps. Repeat the same weight next time.
Form beats weight. A clean rep with lighter weight grows more muscle than a sloppy heavy one.

Lower A: Chest up, sit back, knees track over toes
Don't lock knees hard at top
Squeeze glutes at top, ribs down
Upper A: Pull elbows down, don't lean back much
Lower B: Slight knee bend, push hips back, flat back
Upper B: Full hang to chin over bar
Chest on pad, pull to ribs

weeks.2: Week 2 — RPE 7 (add a little). Same workouts. Add 1–2 reps per set where you can; when you reach the top of a range on all sets, add the smallest weight jump (+1–2.5 kg or next pin). Sets stay the same. Keep tempo controlled — still learning.
weeks.3: Week 3 — RPE 8 (challenge week). Leave about 2 reps in the tank on your last set of each exercise. Add the +1 set option to Goblet Squat, Chest Press and Lat Pulldown if you feel good. If a set feels wobbly, that's your top weight for now.
weeks.4: Week 4 — DELOAD (recover). Use ~60% of Week-3 weights, 2 sets per exercise, stop well short of hard (RPE 5–6). Drop the small isolation moves (lateral raise, face pull, curls, plank) if tired. Focus on smooth form, walking and sleep.

training.cardio: You don't need much. On 1–2 rest days, do 20–30 min of easy incline walking or cycling. The daily step goal already covers most of the fat-loss cardio. Keep intense cardio low so it doesn't eat into gym recovery.

sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours a night, at a consistent time.
Fixed sleep and wake time, even on weekends (±30 min).
No screens 30–45 min before bed; dim the lights.
Last big meal 2–3 hours before bed; caffeine before 3 pm only.
Cool, dark, quiet room. A short 10–20 min nap is fine if nights are short.
hydration: Person 1: ~3.5–4 litres water/day. Person 2: ~2.5–3 litres/day. Add ~500 ml for every hour of training or hot weather.
Drink 500 ml on waking and 500 ml around the workout (before + during).
Urine should be pale yellow. Dark = drink more.
On heavy sweat days, a pinch of salt + lemon in water (or coconut water) replaces electrolytes. Limit sugary drinks and juices — they add hidden calories.

steps.note: Post-dinner 15–20 min walks also help digestion and blood sugar.
steps.hindi: Khaane ke baad walk zaroor karo.

stretching: Hamstring stretch (seated reach) — 30 s each leg
Hip-flexor lunge stretch — 30 s each side
tips: Take rest days seriously — muscle grows on off days, not just in the gym.
Hit your protein every day; it's the #1 recovery tool alongside sleep.
Manage stress (10 min breathing/walk) — high stress slows fat loss and recovery.
If a joint hurts (sharp pain, not normal soreness), swap the exercise and don't push through.
Deload weeks (Week 4) are non-negotiable — they prevent burnout and injury.
Normal muscle soreness for 1–2 days is fine; light movement helps it fade.

supplements.intro: Supplements are a small bonus on top of food, never a replacement. Only these have strong evidence and are worth considering:
rows: 1 scoop (~24 g P) as needed to hit protein target
Convenience only — helps reach 130–180 g protein. Skip if you already hit it from food. Vegans can use soy/pea protein.
Best-studied supplement for strength & muscle; safe long-term. Especially useful for vegetarians. Drink extra water.
Common deficiency in India, esp. indoors; supports bone/muscle. Ideally test first.
Often low on vegetarian diets — worth monitoring and supplementing if low.
Mild performance and focus boost. Not after 3 pm.
supplements.outro: Everything else (fat burners, BCAAs, test boosters) is unnecessary here. Consult a doctor before starting supplements, particularly Vitamin D dosing.

meal_prep: Sunday batch (60–90 min): soak & pressure-cook the week's beans (rajma, chole, kala chana, lobia) and freeze in meal-size boxes; boil and squeeze soya chunks; roast peanuts; make a jar of mint-coriander chutney.
Twice-weekly: chop onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste and store airtight; wash and store greens. Cut prep time to minutes on busy days.
Grains ahead: cook a batch of brown rice/quinoa; refrigerate 3–4 days. Knead atta fresh or store 2 days.
Curd & sprouts: set curd every 2 days; start a sprout jar so a batch is always ready.
Portion as you cook: plate Person 2's base serving first, then add Person 1's extras to the pan/plate — keeps macros on track without weighing every day.
Keep protein visible: pre-portion whey scoops, keep roasted chana/peanuts handy so hitting the protein target is easy.
context.meal_prep_hindi: Ek din pehle taiyari karo — poora hafta easy ho jaata hai.
context.monthly_adjust: If weight isn't moving after 2–3 weeks and steps + protein are on point, drop ~150 kcal (e.g. one less roti/rice serving). If you feel weak or gym numbers crash, you may be cutting too hard — add ~150 kcal back. Re-check body weight and lifts at the end of the month and set up the next block.
